key_insight: Personalized RewardBench introduces a standardized way to evaluate whether reward models capture individual user preferences, enabling measurement of pluralistic alignment rather than one-size-fits-all quality.
problem_solved: Existing RM benchmarks measure general response quality but do not evaluate how well reward models reflect diverse, individual human preferences; this work fills that gap with a dedicated personalization evaluation suite.
method: Define diverse user preference personas and collect human judgments tied to those personas (e.g., pairwise comparisons or preference ratings).
Score candidate responses with reward models conditioned on persona signals and compare predicted rankings to persona-specific human judgments.
Report persona-aware metrics (alignment gaps, calibration, ranking accuracy) and aggregate analyses to reveal model strengths and failure modes.
impact: Provides practitioners a practical benchmark and metrics to diagnose and improve reward models for personalized alignment, supporting safer, more satisfying LLM behavior across diverse users.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: persona → prompt variants → candidate responses → RM scoring → persona-specific evaluation metrics
Heatmap showing RM alignment scores across personas and models (rows: models, columns: personas)
Bar/line chart comparing ranking accuracy and calibration metrics for multiple RMs
Example card: persona description + human-preferred vs model-preferred response side-by-side
paper_title: Personalized RewardBench: Evaluating Reward Models with Human Aligned Personalization
paper_authors: Qiyao Ma, Dechen Gao, Rui Cai, Boqi Zhao, Hanchu Zhou
